correctness.rationale: The stationary generator of the two-dimensional orientation-diffusing ABP with total Poisson reset yields a triangular five-observable moment system. It was reconstructed independently of the published moment expression and algebraically reduced to a positive denominator times a quartic sign polynomial. Its leading, linear and constant coefficients are strictly positive; hence Descartes rule bounds positive roots by two. Positivity at endpoints, a concave-in-activity quadratic and a unique global minimizer prove the exhaustive zero/two-crossing classification including the double-root fold. Derivative signs give the square-root law. Rescaled polynomial limits and coercive lower bounds prove both asymptotic fold regimes. Eighty exact rational cases plus numerical phase and asymptotic checks pass in verify.py. Finite checks alone are not used to infer an infinite root theorem.

value.rationale: For a natural nonequilibrium active-particle model whose original paper shows two numerical confinement crossovers, the theorem establishes the precise global topology of the sign regions for every reset rate, determines the unique minimum activity necessary for any negative-kurtosis regime, describes how the two transitions are born, and gives weak/strong resetting scaling laws. This answers an experimentally interpretable phase-threshold question rather than simply recomputing an already tabulated value. It does not assert a true thermodynamic phase transition.
